question: Can per-token native 8-bit storage at all eight recurrent cache sites lower the physical memory cost of the successful BF16 page reader without changing any qualified short-register output?
protocol: Independent cache-design study responding to the archived BF16 full-length memory loss. Compare the identical recurrent page selector, reader and decoder weights. Control stores original BF16 K/V; candidate encodes every K and V row with native affine 8-bit groups of 64. Keep BF16 page summaries in both; gather selected compressed past rows before native dequantization and fused BF16 attention. The final >=512 input tokens and all generated tokens use every stored position with the original reader mask. Alternate arms over four previously measured 16K/32K original and counterfactual registers; this is an engineering parity test, not independent accuracy evidence. Retain token IDs, actual code and affine tensor byte counts, physical KV offsets and causal attention work. Measure model-resident peak and all selection/conversion/decoding time equally.
gate: All four answers correct for both arms, identical input/output IDs and identified evidence window, correct 8-bit code and scale/bias tensor extents and full physical retention at all eight genuine recurrent KV sites. Peak must fall at least 5% on the full panel, with summed TTFT and end-to-end time each no greater than 1.15 times the BF16 page control. Any miss closes this design. A pass licenses an independent equal-width key swap at physical 131K against untouched Base with all resource gates and an independently authored natural-prose retention study before deployment.
